Activation of RVE/LNK and LWD/TCP genes is crucial for circadian rhythm maintenance and clock output regulation

Activation of RVE/LNK and LWD/TCP genes is crucial for circadian rhythm maintenance and clock output regulation.(A) RVE and LNK family members control various developmental processes in plants, including hypocotyl elongation, starch synthesis and degradation, and double fertilization, by regulating the expression of key genes.(B) RVE and LNK proteins improve resilience to abiotic and biotic stresses by directly regulating the expression of stress-response genes associated with cold and heat responses and with jasmonic acid, salicylic acid, and abscisic acid signaling pathways across multiple species.(C) RVE8, LNK1, and LNK2 regulate the biosynthesis of secondary metabolites such as anthocyanins and phenylpropanoids.(D) TTG1 and TCP proteins are multifunctional regulators with crucial roles in diverse aspects of plant growth and development.(E) LWD and TCP proteins serve as essential regulators of flowering time by controlling the expression of key floral integrator genes such as FT, SOC1, and AP1a in multiple plant species.(F) CHE (TCP21) serves as a versatile regulator of biotic stress responses by directly regulating the expression of genes related to salicylic acid (SA), jasmonic acid (JA), auxin (AUX), and strigolactone (SL) signaling
